body.x: PeoplesHealth Co., Ltd. (CEO Eunsun Kim) participated in CES 2024 held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th (Tuesday) to 12th (Friday, local time).

PeoplesHealth is a company that aims to provide innovative healthcare services to patients who might otherwise be unable to receive treatment due to language and location constraints. The company operates ‘ToggleDoc,’ which supports medical institutions in attracting more patients from overseas, and ‘K-Doc,’ which connects international patients who wish to receive treatment in Korea with Korean hospitals. The goal is to assist more people in accessing the necessary medical care.
At this CES, PeoplesHealth introduced the web application ‘ToggleDoc,’ which effectively manages customers and patients worldwide.

ToggleDoc, providing an intuitive and user-friendly environment, allows for effective management of customers and contracts. This platform enables businesses to streamline their processes and quickly access essential information. Additionally, ToggleDoc automates repetitive and time-consuming tasks, maximizing the efficiency of business processes and reducing workload.

ToggleDoc, with its features like easy communication with customers, workflow optimization, and cost reduction, effectively supports globally distributed patient management, according to the company’s explanation. As a Software as a Service (SaaS) product, ToggleDoc will receive continuous updates. PeoplesHealth is preparing a database that consolidates information on hospitals, medical product prices, and doctor details. While currently being used by institutions attracting foreign patients in Korea for customer management, future updates will expand its functionality to be utilized for patient acquisition regardless of the location of the attracting institution.

A representative stated, “PeoplesHealth participated in CES 2024 to showcase the development and outcomes of our innovative and accessible healthcare services. Our company aims to present innovative technologies and services, overcoming language and location barriers to demonstrate the possibility of easily accessing healthcare services for everyone.” Further explaining, “PeoplesHealth is preparing to introduce our solutions in North America and plans to expand availability to English-speaking countries soon. Our company is working on concrete plans, including establishing a local entity, to enter the U.S. market and expand our business.”

“PeoplesHealth is actively networking with business representatives from North America and Asia during this exhibition. Our company has collaborated with a Taiwanese company, exchanging information about our services related to doctor recommendations and treatment processes. Additionally, positive consultations have occurred with a startup consulting firm in San Francisco. This networking allows PeoplesHealth to explore collaborations and partnerships, enhancing our global presence and potential business expansions.”

CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
